findings.claim: Product defect: toFahrenheit always rounds its result to a whole degree, with no precision parameter and nothing in its signature to show it. By the source, toFahrenheit(36.6) returns 98 rather than about 97.88, and toFahrenheit(21.5) returns 71 rather than about 70.7. This directly violates V-2 (never rounded silently; the caller chooses the precision). It also undermines V-3, because a traveller gets a number that can be off by up to 0.5 degrees F and cannot tell. The sibling toCelsius does not round, so the two directions of the same API treat precision differently. I-1 does not catch this: 100 C converts to exactly 212, so its result is the same with or without Math.round.
findings.cause: tofahrenheit result: value is silently rounded to an integer with no caller-chosen precision

premises.claim: toFahrenheit applies Math.round to c * 9 / 5 + 32 and takes no precision argument, so for c = 100 it computes 212.
toCelsius returns (f - 32) * 5 / 9 with no rounding and takes no precision argument.
